cards.topic: 17.11. Acquiring ownership III — OCCUPATIO and treasure
cards.front: What is OCCUPATIO — which things can be acquired in this way?
cards.back:
Whoever takes possession of a thing belonging to no one (RES NULLIUS) becomes its owner — original acquisition.
• Originally ownerless things (wild animals; pearls and gems from the seabed), derelinquished things (RES DERELICTAE), treasure-trove.
cards.old_front: Was ist OCCUPATIO — welche Sachen können so erworben werden?

cards.topic: 17.11. Acquiring ownership III — OCCUPATIO and treasure
cards.front: What does OCCUPATIO of wild animals require — and when are possession and ownership lost again?
cards.back:
Open and secure possession — given in any case where the captor has direct physical control over the animal (cf Gaius D 41.1.5.1; Proculus D 41.1.55).
• If the animal regains its natural freedom, the captor loses possession AND ownership (Gaius D 41.1.3.2, D 41.1.5 pr).
cards.old_front: Was verlangt die OCCUPATIO wilder Tiere — und wann gehen Besitz und Eigentum wieder verloren?

cards.topic: 17.11. Acquiring ownership III — OCCUPATIO and treasure
cards.front: What role does the CONSUETUDO REVERTENDI play for tamed wild animals?
cards.back:
Animals that are wild by nature but tamed belong to the owner as long as they remain tame and habitually return (CONSUETUDO REVERTENDI) — this is how he exercises control. If they lose the habit, they are wild and ownerless again (Florentinus D 41.1.4; Paulus D 41.2.3.15, 16).
• Swarming bees are wild (anyone may catch them, Gaius D 41.1.5.2); the single bee or pigeon that returns home belongs to the owner.
• For domestic animals it plays no role: runaway domestic animals are not ownerless.
cards.old_front: Welche Rolle spielt die CONSUETUDO REVERTENDI bei gezähmten wilden Tieren?

cards.topic: 17.11. Acquiring ownership III — OCCUPATIO and treasure
cards.front: Paulus D 41.2.3.14 (Case 95): Who owns game in an enclosure, fish in a basin — and game in a fenced forest or fish in a fishpond?
cards.back:
Game in an enclosure and fish in a basin: possession and ownership of whoever caught them and keeps them captive.
• Game in a fenced forest or fish in a pond: possession of the forest/pond does not confer possession of the animals — they are in natural freedom; because of the size of the habitat the owner has no control (→ ownerless).
cards.old_front: Paulus D 41.2.3.14 (Case 95): Wem gehören Wild im Gehege, Fische im Becken — und Wild in einem eingezäunten Wald bzw Fische in einem Fischteich?

cards.topic: 17.11. Acquiring ownership III — OCCUPATIO and treasure
cards.front: When is a thing derelinquished? Does the owner lose ownership of goods jettisoned at sea?
cards.back:
Dereliction = giving up possession with the intention of also giving up ownership → RES DERELICTA, which anyone may occupy (§ 386 S 1 ABGB).
• Jettison: at first only loss of possession; ownership is lost only once the owner regards the goods as abandoned (Iavolenus D 41.1.58, Case 97). In case of doubt, no dereliction (§ 386 S 2 ABGB).
• Ownership is lost irrespective of intention if the thing is removed from human reach to such an extent that it amounts to destruction.
• Classical law: OCCUPATIO of a derelinquished RES MANCIPI confers only bonitarian ownership, civil-law ownership after usucaption.
cards.old_front: Wann ist eine Sache derelinquiert? Verliert der Eigentümer beim Seewurf das Eigentum?

cards.topic: 17.11. Acquiring ownership III — OCCUPATIO and treasure
cards.front: Can one acquire ownership by finding a thing?
cards.back:
Lost (not derelinquished) things cannot be occupied; the finder must give public notice to escape the suspicion of FURTUM (Ulpian D 47.2.43.8, Case 98).
• Mere finding does not allow usucaption either (no IUSTA CAUSA, usually no BONA FIDES).
cards.old_front: Kann man durch Fund Eigentum erwerben?

cards.topic: 17.11. Acquiring ownership III — OCCUPATIO and treasure
cards.front: What is a treasure-trove (THESAURUS) — who owns it according to the different opinions?
cards.back:
A valuable object hidden for so long that its owner can no longer be ascertained (Paulus D 41.1.31.1, Case 99).
• Prevailing view (Sabinians, late classical): RES NULLIUS → acquisition by OCCUPATIO (taking possession).
• Proculians (Neratius, Proculus): if the landowner learns of the treasure, his intention to possess suffices — as possessor he also controls the treasure; no act of seizure needed.
• Older view (Brutus, Manilius): the treasure is a component (ACCESSIO) of the land → belongs to the landowner, no room for OCCUPATIO (Paulus D 41.2.3.3, Case 100).
• Hadrian: half to the finder, half to the landowner (similar to § 399 ABGB).
cards.old_front: Was ist ein Schatz (THESAURUS) — wem gehört er nach den verschiedenen Meinungen?

cards.front: What are fruits (FRUCTUS) — is the child of a slave woman a fruit?
cards.back:
Recurring yields obtained from a thing without diminishing or destroying its substance.
• FRUCTUS NATURALES (milk, wool, eggs) and FRUCTUS CIVILES (e.g. rent).
• PARTUS ANCILLAE (child of a slave woman) is not a fruit; the young of an animal is.
cards.old_front: Was sind Früchte (FRUCTUS) — ist das Kind einer Sklavin eine Frucht?

cards.front: When does the question of ownership of fruits arise — to whom do they belong in principle?
cards.back:
Only after separation (SEPARATIO); before that they are a dependent part of the fruit-bearing thing and share its fate.
• Principle: the owner of the fruit-bearing thing acquires the fruits upon separation.
• Exam tip: grapes/apples = fruits; while growing part of the fruit-bearing thing, upon separation an independent thing.
cards.old_front: Wann stellt sich die Frage nach dem Eigentum an Früchten — wem gehören sie grundsätzlich?

cards.front: How does the BONAE FIDEI POSSESSOR acquire fruits — and why?
cards.back:
With SEPARATIO (e.g. as soon as the apples fall from the tree) — original acquisition.
• BONAE FIDEI POSSESSOR = someone who mistakenly but in good faith believes he is the owner of the fruit-bearing thing.
• Reason: reward for his good faith and his investments.
• If the fruit-bearing thing is pledged, he acquires the fruits free of encumbrances.
cards.old_front: Wie erwirbt der BONAE FIDEI POSSESSOR Früchte — und warum?

cards.front: Paulus D 41.3.4.19 (Case 104): B steals A's sheep and shears them. Variant: B sells them to C, who is in good faith and shears them. Who owns the wool?
cards.back:
Thief B: no ownership of the wool (not a BONAE FIDEI POSSESSOR) and no usucaption — wool shorn with the intention to steal is a RES FURTIVA; moreover, title and good faith are lacking. Even a buyer of the wool from B can acquire neither derivatively nor by usucaption.
• C (good-faith buyer of the sheep): BONAE FIDEI POSSESSOR → acquires the wool upon shearing (SEPARATIO); usucaption is irrelevant.
cards.old_front: Paulus D 41.3.4.19 (Case 104): B stiehlt A's Schafe und schert sie. Variante: B verkauft sie an den gutgläubigen C, der sie schert. Wem gehört die Wolle?

cards.front: How do the emphyteuta, the usufructuary (USUFRUCTUARIUS) and the lessee (COLONUS, CONDUCTOR) acquire fruits?
cards.back:
Emphyteuta (hereditary lessee, heritable right in rem to use land): with SEPARATIO — because of the similarity of emphyteusis to ownership.
USUFRUCTUARIUS (personal, non-heritable servitude): only with PERCEPTIO (gathering, picking); in between, the fruits belong to the owner.
Lessee: likewise only with PERCEPTIO; his acquisition counts as DERIVATIVE (late classical: transfer of ownership by the lessor). If the fruit-bearing thing is pledged, the pledge extends to his fruits.
cards.old_front: Wie erwerben Emphyteuta, Fruchtnießer (USUFRUCTUARIUS) und Pächter (COLONUS, CONDUCTOR) die Früchte?

cards.front: Fruits fall into the hands of a third party before PERCEPTIO. What can the usufructuary or the lessee do?
cards.back:
Only the owner of the fruit-bearing thing can reclaim them (REI VINDICATIO, possibly CONDICTIO FURTIVA).
• Usufructuary: VINDICATIO USUSFRUCTUS against the owner, so that the owner retrieves the fruits for him.
• Lessee: only a contractual claim against the lessor — ACTIO CONDUCTI.
cards.old_front: Früchte fallen vor der PERCEPTIO in die Hände eines Dritten. Was können Fruchtnießer bzw Pächter tun?

cards.front: Example 26: Lessee Aeneas harvests wheat and brings it into his barn; at night Catullus mows the barley, takes the wheat and stores both. Who can reclaim what?
cards.back:
Wheat: belongs to Aeneas (PERCEPTIO) → REI VINDICATIO or CONDICTIO FURTIVA against Catullus.
Barley: after cutting, owned by the landowner Beatus → only Beatus sues (CONDICTIO FURTIVA against the thief, REI VINDICATIO against any possessor); Aeneas can compel him to do so with the ACTIO CONDUCTI.
cards.old_front: Beispiel 26: Pächter Aeneas erntet Weizen und bringt ihn in seine Scheune; nachts mäht Catullus die Gerste, nimmt den Weizen mit und lagert beides. Wer kann was zurückfordern?

cards.front: What does ACCESSIO CEDIT PRINCIPALI mean — where does the rule come from?
cards.back:
The addition follows (legally) the main thing: in a firm connection the fate of the main thing (RES PRINCIPALIS) determines that of the whole; the owner of the main thing acquires the addition and must compensate the former owner.
• Historically derived from SUPERFICIES SOLO CEDIT.
• The owners may agree otherwise (e.g. co-ownership).
• For property law it is irrelevant whether the connection was made in good or bad faith.
cards.old_front: Was besagt ACCESSIO CEDIT PRINCIPALI — woher stammt die Regel?

cards.front: When is a connection inseparable — consequences of a merely severable connection?
cards.back:
Inseparable: separation would cause considerable damage or disproportionate effort; interpenetration of the elements (welding yes, soldering no — the solder separates the metal parts; a tree that draws nutrients from the soil).
• Purpose: preservation of economic value.
Severable connection: no effect in property law; separation by ACTIO AD EXHIBENDUM, then REI VINDICATIO by each owner.
cards.old_front: Wann ist eine Verbindung untrennbar — Folgen einer bloß lösbaren Verbindung?

cards.front: How do the Romans distinguish the main thing from the addition?
cards.back:
By the structure of the ownership action: the main thing is what can be brought to court and vindicated on its own (writing on parchment cannot be vindicated, Paulus D 6.1.23.3, Case 112) — and by common perception (one vindicates “a statue with an arm”, not “an arm with a statue”).
• Value does NOT decide (wool dyed with expensive purple belongs to the owner of the wool); nor does labour.
• Exception according to one opinion: TABULA PICTA.
cards.old_front: Wie unterscheiden die Römer Hauptsache und Zuwachs?

cards.front: Which remedies does someone have who loses his ownership through ACCESSIO?
cards.back:
• If the owner of the whole possesses: ACTIO IN FACTUM (against a good-faith acquirer) or CONDICTIO FURTIVA (whoever connects deliberately with the intention to steal commits FURTUM; alternatively also ACTIO IN FACTUM).
• If the former owner of the addition possesses the whole: against the REI VINDICATIO, EXCEPTIO DOLI → retention until compensation.
• If he made the connection himself, he may also be able to claim the value of his labour.
cards.old_front: Welche Rechtsbehelfe hat, wer sein Eigentum durch ACCESSIO verliert?

cards.front: What is an ACTIO IN FACTUM?
cards.back:
An action granted by the praetor when he sees a need for legal protection but no institutionalised action is available; the formula begins with a description of the concrete facts (FACTUM).
• Umbrella term without specific content (compensation, enforcement of agreements …).
cards.old_front: Was ist eine ACTIO IN FACTUM?

cards.front: Gaius D 41.1.9.1 (Case 110): A writes on B's paper/parchment (even in gold letters). Who owns the result?
cards.back:
B — the paper is the main thing, the writing a mere addition (“paper written on”).
• It is only about ink, gold, paper — not about the intellectual achievement.
• If B sues the possessing A for restitution, A can retain the paper with the EXCEPTIO DOLI until he is compensated for his contribution.
cards.old_front: Gaius D 41.1.9.1 (Case 110): A schreibt auf B's Papier/Pergament (auch in Goldschrift). Wem gehört das Ergebnis?

cards.front: Gaius Inst 2.78 (Case 111): C paints on D's wooden panel (TABULA PICTA). Who owns the painting?
cards.back:
Prevailing opinion in Gaius' time (high classical): the painter — an exception, the artistic achievement prevails.
• The former owner of the panel can ward off the painter's REI VINDICATIO with the EXCEPTIO DOLI (until compensated for the panel); he himself has an ACTIO UTILIS, against which the painter can assert his costs by EXCEPTIO DOLI.
• Gaius himself: like writing on paper → owner of the panel; generally so in late classical law (Paulus D 6.1.23.3).
cards.old_front: Gaius Inst 2.78 (Case 111): C malt auf D's Holztafel (TABULA PICTA). Wem gehört das Bild?

cards.front: Paulus D 6.1.23.5 (Case 113): F's metal arm is (a) soldered, (b) welded onto E's statue. Legal consequences?
cards.back:
(a) Soldering (ADPLUMBATIO): severable → ACTIO AD EXHIBENDUM, then REI VINDICATIO by each owner.
(b) Welding (FERRUMINATIO): inseparable → E acquires the arm (ACCESSIO CEDIT PRINCIPALI); F has the ACTIO IN FACTUM.
• If the welded arm later breaks off, it remains E's property — F's right has been extinguished for good.
cards.old_front: Paulus D 6.1.23.5 (Case 113): Ein Metallarm des F wird an die Statue des E (a) gelötet, (b) geschweißt. Rechtsfolgen?

cards.front: Pomponius (Cassius, Proculus, Pegasus) D 41.1.27.2 (Case 114): Two similar pieces of metal belonging to different owners are welded together. Who owns the whole?
cards.back:
Disputed.
• Cassius: whoever contributed the larger/more valuable piece; if both are equal: co-ownership of the contributors or ownership of the person in whose name the connection was made (cf SPECIFICATIO).
• Proculus and Pegasus: each retains ownership of his part (cf CONFUSIO).
cards.old_front: Pomponius (Cassius, Proculus, Pegasus) D 41.1.27.2 (Case 114): Zwei gleichartige Metallstücke verschiedener Eigentümer werden zusammengeschweißt. Wem gehört das Ganze?

cards.front: What does SUPERFICIES SOLO CEDIT mean; what applies to IMPLANTATIO, SATIO, ALLUVIO?
cards.back:
What is inseparably connected with the land follows its legal fate — the land is always the main thing.
• IMPLANTATIO: D's plant in C's soil belongs to C as soon as it has taken root (Gaius D 41.1.7.13).
• SATIO: A's seed belongs to B as soon as it is sown on B's land.
• ALLUVIO/AVULSIO: deposits belong to the landowner as soon as they have become firmly attached to the land.
• For SATIO and IMPLANTATIO this is final: even harvested grain or an uprooted tree remain with the landowner.
• Compensation: ACTIO IN FACTUM, CONDICTIO FURTIVA or EXCEPTIO DOLI.
cards.old_front: Was bedeutet SUPERFICIES SOLO CEDIT; was gilt bei IMPLANTATIO, SATIO, ALLUVIO?

cards.front: AEDIFICATIO: Why is building a house an exception among the cases of accession?
cards.back:
It combines a severable and an inseparable connection:
• A building with a firm foundation belongs to the landowner (building + land = one entity, vindicable only together).
• Within this entity the house is a severable connection of building materials — but NO ACTIO AD EXHIBENDUM for separation.
• Another's building material: ownership is not extinguished but lies dormant (DOMINIUM DORMIENS) and revives when the building collapses/is demolished (Gaius D 41.1.7.10; Iulianus D 6.1.59).
• Instead of waiting: ACTIO IN FACTUM, CONDICTIO FURTIVA or EXCEPTIO DOLI → after compensation the dormant ownership is extinguished.
cards.old_front: AEDIFICATIO: Warum ist der Hausbau eine Ausnahme unter den Accessionsfällen?

cards.front: Does a movable structure on another's land belong to the landowner (Scaevola D 41.1.60, Case 106)?
cards.back:
No — Titius remains owner of a movable granary that he erected on Seius' field.
• Modern law: superstructure (§ 435 ABGB; cf § 95 Abs 1 BGB) — buildings not meant to remain permanently.
cards.old_front: Gehört ein bewegliches Bauwerk auf fremdem Grund dem Grundeigentümer (Scaevola D 41.1.60, Case 106)?

cards.front: Someone knowingly builds with his own material on another's land — what rights does he have?
cards.back: No claim for compensation (not worthy of protection); only the IUS TOLLENDI: he may remove (parts of) the building, insofar as this does not harm the landowner (Ulpian D 6.1.37, Case 129).
cards.old_front: Wer wissentlich mit eigenem Material auf fremdem Grund baut — welche Rechte hat er?

cards.front: Celsus D 6.1.38 (Case 107): F acquires land in good faith from a non-owner, sows and builds on it; the owner E vindicates. How is F compensated?
cards.back:
1. In principle E must reimburse the expenses — at most up to the increase in value, if this is lower.
2. If E is poor: IUS TOLLENDI of F (demolition and removal of the material); E can avert this by paying what F would gain by the demolition. No chicanery: NEQUE MALITIIS INDULGENDUM EST (no scraping off plaster/paintings merely to destroy).
3. If E intends to sell the land soon and does not pay: F may keep it and pays the estimated value minus what he would have received had he surrendered the building.
cards.old_front: Celsus D 6.1.38 (Case 107): F erwirbt gutgläubig ein Grundstück vom Nichtberechtigten, besät und bebaut es; der Eigentümer E vindiziert. Wie wird F entschädigt?

cards.front: What is the ACTIO DE TIGNO IUNCTO — and what effect does it have on ownership of the material?
cards.back:
Whoever builds on his OWN land with ANOTHER's material must pay the owner of the material double its value (Gaius D 41.1.7.10, Case 108) — only for this constellation, not for building with one's own material on another's land.
• Disputed: purely a penal action → the DUPLUM is a penalty, the (dormant) ownership remains and can be asserted after demolition. (Also) reipersecutory → the DUPLUM is paid in exchange for the material, ownership passes to the builder.
cards.old_front: Was ist die ACTIO DE TIGNO IUNCTO — und welche Wirkung hat sie aufs Eigentum am Material?

cards.topic: 17.11. Acquiring ownership III — CONFUSIO, COMMIXTIO, mixing money
cards.front: What are the legal consequences of mixing/blending similar things belonging to different owners (without consent)?
cards.back:
No change in the ownership rights: each can immediately claim, by VINDICATIO PRO PARTE, the share corresponding to his contribution (quantity or value) (Pomponius in Ulpian D 6.1.3.2, D 6.1.5.1).
• No ACTIO AD EXHIBENDUM needed; no compensation claims needed.
• Gold alloyed with copper: by value — the owner of the gold receives more of the alloy.
• A practical solution that ignores the identity of the individual grains.
cards.old_front: Welche Rechtsfolgen hat das Vermischen/Vermengen gleichartiger Sachen verschiedener Eigentümer (ohne Einverständnis)?

cards.topic: 17.11. Acquiring ownership III — CONFUSIO, COMMIXTIO, mixing money
cards.front: Mixing by mutual consent — what applies?
cards.back:
The mixture is in co-ownership (COMMUNIO) of all contributors (Gaius D 41.1.7.8; Pomponius in Ulpian D 6.1.5 pr).
• Dissolution by the ACTIO COMMUNI DIVIDUNDO (settlement of accounts, division, allotment); then REI VINDICATIO for the allotted share.
• Difference from unintentional mixing: there VINDICATIO PRO PARTE.
cards.old_front: Vermischung mit gegenseitigem Einverständnis — was gilt?

cards.topic: 17.11. Acquiring ownership III — CONFUSIO, COMMIXTIO, mixing money
cards.front: What applies when A mixes B's money indistinguishably with his own?
cards.back:
A becomes ORIGINAL sole owner of all the money (Iavolenus (Cassius) D 46.3.78, Case 119) — whether in good or bad faith, even a thief.
• Octavenus (Paulus D 6.1.6): VINDICATIO PRO PARTE conceivable as long as all the coins are still with A; it fails as soon as some have been given away.
• B: compensation — against a good-faith A an enrichment action (e.g. CONDICTIO INDEBITI), against a thief CONDICTIO FURTIVA.
• Reason: flexible cash management in commerce; coins are hard to trace.
cards.old_front: Was gilt, wenn A fremdes Geld des B ununterscheidbar mit eigenem vermengt?

cards.topic: 17.11. Acquiring ownership III — CONFUSIO, COMMIXTIO, mixing money
cards.front: In which two ways does one acquire original ownership of another's money (NUMMOS CONSUMERE)?
cards.back:
1. Indistinguishable mixing with one's own money.
2. Spending another's money in good faith — the owner cannot vindicate against the recipient.
• Both are called NUMMOS CONSUMERE (“using up” coins).
• Cf § 371 ABGB.
cards.old_front: Auf welche zwei Arten erwirbt man originär Eigentum an fremdem Geld (NUMMOS CONSUMERE)?

cards.front: SPECIFICATIO vs mere processing vs ACCESSIO — how to distinguish them, with examples?
cards.back:
SPECIFICATIO: creative transformation of another's thing into a thing of a different kind (different appearance, different name) — Marcus makes clothes out of Titus' wool.
Processing: no substantial change → no consequence in property law — Seius cleans Titus' wool.
ACCESSIO: Rufus dyes Titus' wool with his own purple.
cards.old_front: SPECIFICATIO vs bloße Bearbeitung vs ACCESSIO — Abgrenzung mit Beispielen?

cards.front: Sabinians vs Proculians on SPECIFICATIO — reasoning?
cards.back:
Sabinians: identity is determined by the material (MATERIA MANENS) — without material no thing (QUIA SINE MATERIA NULLA SPECIES EFFICI POSSIT) → the product belongs to the owner of the material.
Proculians: identity is determined by the form — the old thing perishes, the new one is initially a RES NULLIUS (QUIA QUOD FACTUM EST, ANTEA NULLIUS FUERAT) → the maker acquires by OCCUPATIO.
• Source: Gaius D 41.1.7.7 (Case 120).
cards.old_front: Sabinianer vs Prokulianer bei der SPECIFICATIO — Begründung?

cards.front: What does the MEDIA SENTENTIA say on SPECIFICATIO — details?
cards.back:
Reversible → Sabinian: the product belongs to the owner of the material (abstract criterion: theoretical reversibility suffices; example: metal).
Irreversible → Proculian: the maker (or whoever has it made in his name, ALIENO NOMINE) acquires originally; old rights are extinguished.
• Only without the consent of those involved: under a contract for work (LOCATIO CONDUCTIO OPERIS) ownership remains with the customer who supplies the material.
cards.old_front: Was besagt die MEDIA SENTENTIA zur SPECIFICATIO — Details?

cards.front: Gaius D 41.1.7.7 (Case 120): Which examples does Gaius give — how are they to be solved under the MEDIA SENTENTIA?
cards.back:
• Vessel made from another's gold/copper/silver → reversible (can be melted down) → owner of the material.
• Ship, cupboard, chair made from another's planks; clothes from another's wool; mead from another's honey and wine; salve from another's medicinal substances; oil from another's olives; wine from another's grapes → irreversible → maker.
• Threshing another's grain → the grains belong to the owner of the ears: no new thing, merely uncovering what already exists.
cards.old_front: Gaius D 41.1.7.7 (Case 120): Welche Beispiele nennt Gaius — wie sind sie nach der MEDIA SENTENTIA zu lösen?

cards.front: Which remedies does someone have who loses his ownership through SPECIFICATIO (or ACCESSIO) — good-faith vs bad-faith acquirer?
cards.back:
Good-faith maker: ACTIO IN FACTUM for compensation.
Bad-faith maker: CONDICTIO FURTIVA.
• If the former owner of the material possesses the product: EXCEPTIO DOLI against the maker's REI VINDICATIO until he is paid the value of the material.
• In the case of reversible transformation the maker acquires nothing, but can claim the increase in value due to his labour (ACTIO IN FACTUM or EXCEPTIO DOLI).
cards.old_front: Welche Rechtsbehelfe hat, wer durch SPECIFICATIO (oder ACCESSIO) sein Eigentum verliert — gut- vs bösgläubiger Erwerber?

cards.front: [Textbook Ex 35] Bellona has leased a garden and farm buildings from Ago. Carus collects the windfall under the trees, picks an entire apple tree bare and steals a crate of pears that Bellona had picked and stored in the cellar. Who owns the windfall, the picked apples and the pears? Which actions does Bellona have?
cards.back:
Windfall and apples picked by Carus: owned by the lessor Ago — the lessee acquires only with PERCEPTIO; upon separation the fruits fall to the owner of the fruit-bearing thing.
Pears: owned by Bellona (she picked them = PERCEPTIO).
• Bellona: for the pears REI VINDICATIO or CONDICTIO FURTIVA + ACTIO FURTI against Carus.
• For the windfall and apples only Ago can vindicate or bring the condictio; Bellona can compel him to do so with the ACTIO CONDUCTI (cf Example 26).

cards.front: [Textbook Ex 36] Kassandra orders her slave Leo to catch hares in her neighbour's forest. Leo catches two and puts them in a basket; on Kassandra's extensive grounds he drops the basket — one hare disappears into the bushes, the other stays in the basket and is brought to Kassandra. Possession and ownership of the hares?
cards.back:
• Wild hares are RES NULLIUS; the fact that they live in the neighbour's forest does not make them her property (Paulus D 41.2.3.14).
• With Leo's catch (IUSSUM) Kassandra acquires possession and ownership (OCCUPATIO, ANIMO NOSTRO CORPORE ALIENO) — in the basket there is open, secure control.
• Hare 1: by fleeing into the bushes it regains its natural freedom → Kassandra loses possession and ownership; on her extensive grounds she has no control (cf fenced forest).
• Hare 2: remains in Kassandra's possession and ownership.

cards.front: [Textbook Ex 37] In a house he has inherited, Merops finds wooden planks, from which he builds a cupboard, and a bronze statue of Mars, which he has a goldsmith melt down and make into a statue of Iustitia. The planks and the statue had only been given to his uncle for safekeeping. Ownership of the cupboard and the statue?
cards.back:
Cupboard: irreversible SPECIFICATIO (Gaius D 41.1.7.7: cupboard made from another's planks) → Merops acquires originally; the owner of the planks has (Merops being in good faith) the ACTIO IN FACTUM.
Iustitia statue: metal is reversible (can be melted down) → remains the property of the owner of the Mars statue → REI VINDICATIO; Merops (in whose name the work was done) can assert the increase in value by EXCEPTIO DOLI.
• Merops does not inherit things belonging to others: the uncle was only a depositary.

Bretter und Statue waren dem Onkel nur zur Verwahrung gegeben. Eigentum an Schrank und Statue?

cards.front: [Textbook Ex 38] Faustilla welds four legs onto her tabletop, one of which belongs to Cleo, and screws on strips belonging to Iris. Which actions do Cleo and Iris have against Faustilla, who is in possession? What if Faustilla knew that she was using another's material? What if she is mentally ill?
cards.back:
Cleo (leg welded = inseparable): Faustilla acquires the leg (ACCESSIO CEDIT PRINCIPALI, tabletop = main thing) → Cleo: ACTIO IN FACTUM for compensation.
Iris (strips screwed on = severable): remains owner → ACTIO AD EXHIBENDUM, then REI VINDICATIO.
• If Faustilla knew (intention to steal): acquisition of ownership nonetheless (good/bad faith irrelevant), but FURTUM → Cleo: CONDICTIO FURTIVA (or ACTIO IN FACTUM), plus ACTIO FURTI; Iris: as above + ACTIO FURTI.
• Mentally ill: no DOLUS possible (no delictual capacity) → no FURTUM; in property law the accession stands → ACTIO IN FACTUM.

Welche Klagen haben Cleo und Iris gegen die besitzende Faustilla? Was, wenn Faustilla wusste, dass sie fremdes Material verwendet? Was, wenn sie geisteskrank ist?

cards.front: [Textbook Ex 39] The painter Menander paints the portrait of the empress on a wooden panel given to him by Florentinus (Florentinus bought it in good faith more than a year ago from Brutus, who had stolen it from Eros) and drapes it in his own cloth (value 50), which he dyes with Xanthippe's purple (value 20,000). Who owns (a) the purple cloth, (b) the painted panel?
cards.back:
(a) Cloth: Menander — dyed wool/cloth belongs to the owner of the cloth; the value of the purple does not decide. Xanthippe: ACTIO IN FACTUM (if intentional, CONDICTIO FURTIVA).
(b) Panel: Eros remained owner — stolen (RES FURTIVA), hence no usucaption by Florentinus despite good faith and more than a year; Florentinus could transfer nothing.
• TABULA PICTA: according to the prevailing opinion in Gaius' time the painting belongs to the painter Menander (Eros: ACTIO UTILIS or EXCEPTIO DOLI for compensation for the panel); according to Gaius and late classical doctrine (Paulus D 6.1.23.3) to the owner of the panel, Eros (Menander: EXCEPTIO DOLI for his costs).
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 39] Maler Menander malt auf eine Holztafel, die ihm Florentinus geschenkt hat (Florentinus kaufte sie vor über einem Jahr gutgläubig von Brutus, der sie Eros gestohlen hatte), das Bild der Kaiserin und drapiert es in eigenes Tuch (Wert 50), das er mit Purpur der Xanthippe (Wert 20.000) färbt. Wem gehören (a) das Purpurtuch, (b) die bemalte Tafel?

cards.front: [Textbook Ex 40] Nike builds on her own land and inadvertently uses two beams belonging to her neighbour Orion. Orion, with his own material, builds a stable with a foundation and a dog kennel on land belonging to Pius. (a) Orion's rights concerning the beams? (b) Who owns the stable and the kennel? (c) What can Pius do against Orion, and what can Orion object?
cards.back:
(a) Orion's ownership of the beams lies dormant (DOMINIUM DORMIENS), no action for separation. He can await demolition or sue immediately: ACTIO DE TIGNO IUNCTO (building on one's own land with another's material → double value) or compensation by ACTIO IN FACTUM.
(b) Stable (firm foundation) → Pius (SUPERFICIES SOLO CEDIT). Dog kennel (movable) → remains Orion's (cf Scaevola D 41.1.60).
(c) Pius: REI VINDICATIO for the land together with the stable. Orion: if he was in good faith, EXCEPTIO DOLI for reimbursement of expenses up to the increase in value, or IUS TOLLENDI (Celsus D 6.1.38); if he knowingly built on another's land, only IUS TOLLENDI (Ulpian D 6.1.37).

cards.front: [Textbook Ex 41] The wine merchant Daphne mixes red wine of the same quality from two barrels. The next day she learns that her steward had sold and delivered the wine in one of the barrels to Eros. Who owns the mixed wine? FURTUM? Remedies and compensation for Eros?
cards.back:
• CONFUSIO without consent: ownership remains unaffected — Eros owns the share corresponding to his barrel, Daphne the rest.
• No FURTUM: Daphne knew nothing, no intention to enrich herself (DOLUS is lacking).
• Eros: VINDICATIO PRO PARTE (no ACTIO AD EXHIBENDUM needed).
• Compensation: not needed — the VINDICATIO PRO PARTE safeguards his interests (with equal quality, by quantity).

cards.front: [Textbook Ex 42] Before a journey Ismene gives Quartus a silver plate, wine, honey and hazelnuts for safekeeping; Quartus mistakenly thinks they are a gift. He has the plate reworked into a vase, makes mead out of the wine and honey and cracks the nuts. What can Ismene claim? Difference if he ground the nuts?
cards.back:
• No derivative acquisition: no common causa (deposit vs gift) → Ismene initially remains owner.
• Vase: metal reversible → Ismene remains owner → REI VINDICATIO; Quartus: EXCEPTIO DOLI for the increase in value he created.
• Mead: irreversible (Gaius D 41.1.7.7) → Quartus acquires originally; in good faith → Ismene: ACTIO IN FACTUM for compensation.
• Cracked nuts: like threshing — merely uncovering, no new thing → Ismene remains owner of the kernels (REI VINDICATIO).
• Ground: probably irreversible transformation into something new → Quartus owner, Ismene ACTIO IN FACTUM (solution derived from the MEDIA SENTENTIA).

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Formulary procedure (IN IURE / APUD IUDICEM)
cards.front: Capacity to sue and capacity to be sued in an ACTIO IN REM — who is plaintiff, who is defendant?
cards.back:
Plaintiff: whoever asserts a right in rem (capacity to sue).
Defendant: whoever POSSESSES the thing in dispute and denies the plaintiff's right (capacity to be sued).
• E.g. (Ex 27 in the text): Agatha sues Cara, who does not possess the sheep (it is with Bolos) → the action fails.
• Relative claims → ACTIONES IN PERSONAM (law of obligations).
cards.old_front: Aktivlegitimation und Passivlegitimation bei der ACTIO IN REM — wer ist Kläger, wer Beklagter?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Formulary procedure (IN IURE / APUD IUDICEM)
cards.front: Into which two stages is the Roman formulary procedure divided — and why?
cards.back:
1. Proceedings IN IURE before the PRAETOR.
2. Proceedings APUD IUDICEM before the IUDEX.
• Purpose: relieving the praetor in a growing society while preserving his influence on the interpretation and development of the civil law.
cards.old_front: In welche zwei Abschnitte gliedert sich der römische Formularprozess — warum?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Formulary procedure (IN IURE / APUD IUDICEM)
cards.front: Who is the PRAETOR, what is his edict? PRAETOR URBANUS vs PEREGRINUS?
cards.back:
Magistrate responsible for the administration of justice in Rome, elected for one year; grants ACTIONES and EXCEPTIONES.
• Edict at the start of his term of office: promise of legal protection + catalogue of formulae of all actions and defences.
• Since 242 BC two praetors: URBANUS (disputes between citizens, IUS CIVILE), PEREGRINUS (with/between foreigners, IUS GENTIUM).
• Under Hadrian final version of the edict (around AD 130).
cards.old_front: Wer ist der PRAETOR, was ist sein Edikt? PRAETOR URBANUS vs PEREGRINUS?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Formulary procedure (IN IURE / APUD IUDICEM)
cards.front: Which three options does the praetor have in the proceedings IN IURE?
cards.back:
1. The edict contains a suitable ACTIO → he grants it (the formula determines the proceedings).
2. No suitable ACTIO, but a legitimate request → ACTIO IN FACTUM or ACTIO UTILIS (often modelled on, EXEMPLUM, an edictal action — analogy).
3. Inadmissible request → refusal (DENEGATIO ACTIONIS).
cards.old_front: Welche drei Möglichkeiten hat der Prätor im Verfahren IN IURE?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Formulary procedure (IN IURE / APUD IUDICEM)
cards.front: What is the LITIS CONTESTATIO?
cards.back:
Conclusion of the proceedings IN IURE: the praetor appoints the IUDEX and issues the procedural formula (ACTIO + any EXCEPTIONES) as the programme for the further proceedings.
• Probably “witnessing of the dispute” (written witnessed record of the procedural programme).
cards.old_front: Was ist die LITIS CONTESTATIO?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Formulary procedure (IN IURE / APUD IUDICEM)
cards.front: What is the purpose of an EXCEPTIO, and who bears the burden of proof for INTENTIO and EXCEPTIO?
cards.back:
A defence (plea) of the defendant where the ACTIO would succeed according to its wording, but reasons outside it speak for the defendant (e.g. EXCEPTIO DOLI in D 39.5.25).
• Stands in the formula immediately after the INTENTIO; formulates negative requirements of the claim.
• Burden of proof: INTENTIO → plaintiff; EXCEPTIO → defendant.
cards.old_front: Wozu dient eine EXCEPTIO, und wer trägt die Beweislast für INTENTIO und EXCEPTIO?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Formulary procedure (IN IURE / APUD IUDICEM)
cards.front: Why is the procedural formula a “hypothetical judgment” — what does the IUDEX do?
cards.back:
The praetor grants ACTIO/EXCEPTIO solely on the basis of the allegations, without examining them: “If it appears that … , condemn; if not, acquit.”
• The IUDEX is a private individual (not an official), establishes which allegations are true and decides according to the formula — comparable to a juror; he does not resolve questions of law.
cards.old_front: Warum ist die Prozessformel ein „hypothetisches Urteil“ — was macht der IUDEX?

cards.front: Which three actions protect ownership?
cards.back:
1. REI VINDICATIO — civil-law owner who has lost possession, against the possessor.
2. ACTIO PUBLICIANA — the same purpose for the usucapient (and the bonitarian owner).
3. ACTIO NEGATORIA — against other interferences by third parties.
cards.old_front: Mit welchen drei Klagen wird Eigentum geschützt?

cards.front: What is the wording of the formula of the REI VINDICATIO, and what are its parts called?
cards.back:
(1) INTENTIO: SI PARET REM, QUA DE AGITUR, EX IURE QUIRITIUM AULI AGERII ESSE — if it appears that the thing belongs to the plaintiff under quiritary law,
(2) CLAUSULA ARBITRARIA: NEQUE EA RES RESTITUETUR — and it is not restored,
(3) CONDEMNATIO: QUANTI EA RES ERIT, TANTAM PECUNIAM IUDEX NUMERIUM NEGIDIUM AULO AGERIO CONDEMNATO, SI NON PARET ABSOLVITO.
• AULUS AGERIUS / NUMERIUS NEGIDIUS = placeholder names for plaintiff/defendant.
cards.old_front: Wie lautet die Formel der REI VINDICATIO, und wie heißen ihre Teile?

cards.front: Who can bring the REI VINDICATIO? Can the bonitarian owner (e.g. Alcesimus)?
cards.back:
Only whoever asserts quirite ownership (DOMINIUM EX IURE QUIRITIUM) — as the INTENTIO says.
• Alcesimus buys a slave, merely delivered by traditio; stolen two months later → no REI VINDICATIO: during the usucaption period he is only bonitarian owner. He has the ACTIO PUBLICIANA.
cards.old_front: Wer kann die REI VINDICATIO erheben? Kann es der bonitarische Eigentümer (Bsp Alcesimus)?

cards.front: What is the PROBATIO DIABOLICA?
cards.back:
The “devilish proof” of civil-law ownership: the plaintiff must prove that he acquired from the civil-law owner, who in turn acquired from a civil-law owner, and so on — back to an original acquisition (e.g. USUCAPIO).
• Mitigated in practice because the IUDEX was not bound by any rules of evidence; the ACTIO PUBLICIANA avoids it.
cards.old_front: Was ist die PROBATIO DIABOLICA?

cards.front: To what does the IUDEX condemn in the REI VINDICATIO — what does the CLAUSULA ARBITRARIA achieve?
cards.back:
Always to money (OMNIS CONDEMNATIO PECUNIARIA EST) — to the estimated value at the time of judgment (QUANTI EA RES ERIT); never to return of the thing.
• CLAUSULA ARBITRARIA: only someone who does not restore is condemned → after proof of ownership, an order to restore (IUSSUM DE RESTITUENDO); return together with the fruits prevents condemnation.
• If the defendant maliciously refuses to return, the plaintiff estimates the value under oath (IUSIURANDUM IN LITEM).
cards.old_front: Wozu verurteilt der IUDEX bei der REI VINDICATIO — was bewirkt die CLAUSULA ARBITRARIA?

cards.front: What is the EXCEPTIO DOLI — PRAETERITI (SPECIALIS) vs PRAESENTIS (GENERALIS)?
cards.back:
Formula: SI IN EA RE NIHIL DOLO MALO AULI AGERII FACTUM SIT NEQUE FIAT — if the plaintiff has not acted and does not act fraudulently.
• DOLI PRAETERITI (SPECIALIS): fraud in the past, e.g. right acquired fraudulently.
• DOLI PRAESENTIS (GENERALIS): bringing the action itself is fraudulent.
• E.g. Tullius/Cato: Tullius knowingly obtains by deceit the MANCIPATIO of the wrong estate and vindicates → DOLI PRAETERITI; if he only realises the mistake later and sues nonetheless → DOLI PRAESENTIS.
cards.old_front: Was ist die EXCEPTIO DOLI — PRAETERITI (SPECIALIS) vs PRAESENTIS (GENERALIS)?

cards.front: Whom does the EXCEPTIO REI VENDITAE ET TRADITAE protect?
cards.back:
The bonitarian owner to whom the civil-law owner has sold and (merely) delivered a RES MANCIPI: if the seller — who remains quirite owner until the end of the usucaption period — vindicates against him, he wards off the REI VINDICATIO with the EXCEPTIO REI VENDITAE ET TRADITAE.
• Only for acquisition by PURCHASE; for another IUSTA CAUSA TRADITIONIS → EXCEPTIO DOLI. (Textbook p. 160)
cards.old_front: Wen schützt die EXCEPTIO REI VENDITAE ET TRADITAE?

cards.front: Must the defendant in a REI VINDICATIO be in possession? Who are FICTI POSSESSORES?
cards.back:
Yes, only the possessor can be condemned.
• Exception: whoever fraudulently defends the action without possessing (QUI LITI SE OBTULIT, Paulus D 6.1.7 — e.g. to cover for the true possessor), or fraudulently gives up possession after the LITIS CONTESTATIO → PRO POSSESSIONE DOLUS EST.
• They are condemned as fictitious possessors (FICTI POSSESSORES).
• Fiction = deliberate assumption of non-existent facts in order to trigger a legal consequence.
cards.old_front: Muss der Beklagte der REI VINDICATIO besitzen? Wer sind FICTI POSSESSORES?

cards.front: What is the wording of the formula of the EXCEPTIO REI VENDITAE ET TRADITAE?
cards.back:
SI NON AULUS AGERIUS FUNDUM, QUO DE AGITUR, NUMERIO NEGIDIO VENDIDIT ET TRADIDIT — “if the plaintiff has not sold and delivered the land in dispute to the defendant”.
• The defence therefore applies only if the plaintiff himself sold AND delivered. (Textbook p. 160)
cards.old_front: Wie lautet die Formel der EXCEPTIO REI VENDITAE ET TRADITAE?

cards.front: EXCEPTIO REI VENDITAE ET TRADITAE or EXCEPTIO DOLI — when does the bonitarian owner defend himself with which defence?
cards.back:
EXCEPTIO REI VENDITAE ET TRADITAE only if his acquisition is based on a PURCHASE (EMPTIO VENDITIO) — that is what the formula says.
• If the acquisition is based on another IUSTA CAUSA TRADITIONIS (e.g. gift, dowry), the formula does not fit → he raises the EXCEPTIO DOLI. (Textbook p. 160)
cards.old_front: EXCEPTIO REI VENDITAE ET TRADITAE oder EXCEPTIO DOLI — wann wehrt sich der bonitarische Eigentümer mit welcher Einrede?

cards.front: Against whom is the REI VINDICATIO directed? What does UBI REM MEAM INVENIO, IBI VINDICO mean?
cards.back:
Against the POSSESSOR: the REI VINDICATIO is the action of the (quirite) owner who does not possess against the non-owner in possession — against anyone who possesses.
• Maxim: UBI REM MEAM INVENIO, IBI VINDICO — wherever I find my thing, there I vindicate it.
• Requirement: the thing still exists. (Textbook p. 160)
cards.old_front: Gegen wen richtet sich die REI VINDICATIO? Was bedeutet UBI REM MEAM INVENIO, IBI VINDICO?

cards.front: When is ownership lost, so that a REI VINDICATIO is no longer possible?
cards.back:
• When the thing has perished (been destroyed).
• When someone other than the plaintiff has acquired ORIGINAL ownership of it. (Textbook p. 160)
cards.old_front: Wann ist das Eigentum verloren, sodass keine REI VINDICATIO mehr möglich ist?

cards.front: With which interdicts does one clarify, before a REI VINDICATIO, who possesses — and whom do they help?
cards.back:
They clarify the preliminary question of who has IUSTA POSSESSIO:
• INTERDICTUM UTI POSSIDETIS (land) → whoever LAST possessed without flaw (IUSTA POSSESSIO) wins.
• INTERDICTUM UTRUBI (movables) → whoever possessed without flaw for the LONGEST time in the LAST YEAR wins. (Textbook p. 160)
cards.old_front: Mit welchen Interdikten klärt man vor einer REI VINDICATIO, wer besitzt — und wem helfen sie?

cards.front: Possessory interdicts (UTI POSSIDETIS, UTRUBI) or ACTIONES IN REM — what does each clarify?
cards.back:
Interdicts are purely POSSESSORY: they only clarify who has IUSTA POSSESSIO IN RELATION to the other.
• Rights IN REM (ownership, limited rights in rem) are clarified by the ACTIONES IN REM (petitory).
• Likewise today: action for disturbance of possession § 339 ABGB in conjunction with §§ 454 ff ZPO (possessory) vs REI VINDICATIO § 366 ABGB, ACTIO PUBLICIANA § 372 ABGB (petitory). (Textbook p. 161 + fn 9)
cards.old_front: Besitzinterdikte (UTI POSSIDETIS, UTRUBI) oder ACTIONES IN REM — was klären sie jeweils?

cards.front: Why is the role of the defendant more favourable in proceedings IN REM?
cards.back:
Because the BURDEN OF PROOF lies with the plaintiff: he must prove his ownership.
• It therefore pays to obtain possession first by a possessory interdict — then the opponent has to sue. (Textbook p. 161, Ex 31)
cards.old_front: Warum ist im Prozess IN REM die Rolle des Beklagten günstiger?

cards.front: Can the possessor be compelled to defend a REI VINDICATIO (LITIS CONTESTATIO)?
cards.back:
No. ACTIONES IN REM create NO duty to defend: the defendant cannot be compelled to take part in the LITIS CONTESTATIO and become a party to the proceedings.
• Pressure is created only by the ACTIO AD EXHIBENDUM (movables) or the INTERDICTUM QUEM FUNDUM (land). (Textbook p. 161)
cards.old_front: Kann der Besitzer gezwungen werden, sich auf eine REI VINDICATIO einzulassen (LITIS CONTESTATIO)?

cards.front: How does the ACTIO AD EXHIBENDUM prepare the REI VINDICATIO if the possessor refuses to defend?
cards.back:
The plaintiff demands that the defendant produce (exhibit) the thing IN IURE.
→ If he does NOT produce it: condemnation to a fine amounting to the value of the thing.
→ If he produces it but refuses to defend the REI VINDICATIO: the praetor allows the plaintiff to take the thing away. (Textbook p. 161)
cards.old_front: Wie bereitet die ACTIO AD EXHIBENDUM die REI VINDICATIO vor, wenn der Besitzer sich nicht einlassen will?

cards.front: Is the ACTIO AD EXHIBENDUM an ACTIO IN REM?
cards.back:
No — an ACTIO IN PERSONAM, which creates a DUTY TO DEFEND.
• In this way it supports and complements the REI VINDICATIO (which itself imposes no duty to defend). (Textbook p. 161)
cards.old_front: Ist die ACTIO AD EXHIBENDUM eine ACTIO IN REM?

cards.front: What is the INTERDICTUM QUEM FUNDUM?
cards.back:
The counterpart of the ACTIO AD EXHIBENDUM for LAND: it puts the possessor of land under pressure to defend the plaintiff's REI VINDICATIO.
• Movable thing → ACTIO AD EXHIBENDUM; land → INTERDICTUM QUEM FUNDUM. (Textbook p. 161)
cards.old_front: Was ist das INTERDICTUM QUEM FUNDUM?

cards.front: Ulpianus (Pegasus) D 6.1.9 (Case 121): Which possessors can be sued with the REI VINDICATIO?
cards.back:
Pegasus (early classical): only those with interdictal possession (proprietary possessors and natural possessors protected by interdicts).
Ulpian (late classical): what matters is the FACULTAS RESTITUENDI → also natural possessors without interdictal protection, provided they are able to return the thing.
cards.old_front: Ulpianus (Pegasus) D 6.1.9 (Case 121): Welche Besitzer können mit der REI VINDICATIO beklagt werden?

cards.front: What does the principle of RESTITUERE mean — which fruits does the successful vindicant receive?
cards.back:
The plaintiff is to be placed as if the thing had been returned to him at the LITIS CONTESTATIO.
• Hence all yields between LITIS CONTESTATIO and judgment: FRUCTUS PERCEPTI (gathered) and FRUCTUS PERCIPIENDI/NEGLECTI (those that could have been gathered; Paulus D 6.1.33).
• Applies irrespective of good faith.
• E.g.: Peitho earns 100, Seneca would have earned 150 → Seneca receives the estate + 150.
cards.old_front: Was bedeutet das Prinzip des RESTITUERE — welche Früchte erhält der siegreiche Vindikant?

cards.front: What applies to fruits the defendant gathered BEFORE the LITIS CONTESTATIO?
cards.back:
Here good faith counts: the BONAE FIDEI POSSESSOR acquires them with SEPARATIO (on subsequent bad faith: Julian vs Pomponius/Paulus).
• The MALAE FIDEI POSSESSOR commits FURTUM by taking them → compensation of value (CONDICTIO FURTIVA) + penalty (ACTIO FURTI); existing fruits probably also by REI VINDICATIO.
cards.old_front: Was gilt für Früchte, die der Beklagte VOR der LITIS CONTESTATIO gezogen hat?

cards.front: The thing in dispute perishes between LITIS CONTESTATIO and judgment. Is the defendant liable? (Liability models)
cards.back:
Grounds: DOLUS (intent), CULPA (negligence), CASUS (chance).
• Principle: without possession no condemnation — except in the case of DOLUS (fiction of possession; Paulus D 6.1.27.1).
• Proculians (RESTITUERE, wording of the formula NEQUE EA RES RESTITUETUR): always liable, even for CASUS — had it been returned at the LC, the thing would not have perished.
• Sabinians: liable for any fault (DOLUS or CULPA; Ulpian D 6.1.15.3) — as in the law of delict (LEX AQUILIA).
cards.old_front: Die streitige Sache geht zwischen LITIS CONTESTATIO und Urteil unter. Haftet der Beklagte? (Haftungsmodelle)

cards.front: Paulus D 6.1.16.1 (Case 126): After the LITIS CONTESTATIO, B sends the vindicated ship to sea in a favourable season; it sinks. Is B liable?
cards.back:
No — no negligence if he sails in the sailing season; Paulus holds liable only for CULPA (and DOLUS, ARGUMENTUM A MINORE AD MAIUS).
• Liable, however, if he entrusts the ship to “less suitable persons”: CULPA IN ELIGENDO.
• Leaving it in the harbour does not help: the possessor need not leave the thing unused and is in any case liable for FRUCTUS PERCIPIENDI.
cards.old_front: Paulus D 6.1.16.1 (Case 126): B schickt das vindizierte Schiff nach der LITIS CONTESTATIO zu günstiger Jahreszeit auf See; es sinkt. Haftet B?

cards.front: What claims does the BONAE FIDEI POSSESSOR have against the vindicating owner on account of his expenses?
cards.back:
Reimbursement of value-increasing expenses (IMPENSAE), enforced by retention (RETENTIO) until full payment.
• Procedurally: EXCEPTIO DOLI (PRAESENTIS) against the REI VINDICATIO — as long as the owner does not pay, his action is fraudulent.
• Cf § 471 Abs 1 ABGB (right of retention).
cards.old_front: Welche Ansprüche hat der BONAE FIDEI POSSESSOR gegen den vindizierenden Eigentümer wegen seiner Aufwendungen?

cards.front: Ulpianus (Iulianus) D 6.1.37 (Case 129): A good-faith possessor of land learns that the land belongs to a third party, and only then builds a house. Rights against the vindicating owner?
cards.back:
No EXCEPTIO DOLI for reimbursement — he was no longer in good faith when building began.
• All he has left is the IUS TOLLENDI (right of removal) regarding the house he built.
• Cf Celsus D 6.1.38 (Case 107) on the good-faith builder.
cards.old_front: Ulpianus (Iulianus) D 6.1.37 (Case 129): Ein gutgläubiger Grundstücksbesitzer erfährt, dass das Grundstück einem Dritten gehört, und baut erst danach ein Haus. Rechte gegen den vindizierenden Eigentümer?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — ACTIO PUBLICIANA, pleas, ACTIO NEGATORIA
cards.front: What is the wording of the INTENTIO of the ACTIO PUBLICIANA — on which fiction is it based?
cards.back:
SI QUEM HOMINEM AULUS AGERIUS EMIT ET IS EI TRADITUS EST, ANNO POSSEDISSET, TUM SI EUM HOMINEM … EIUS EX IURE QUIRITIUM ESSE OPORTERET — if the slave bought and delivered would be the buyer's quirite property, had the buyer possessed him for a year …
• Fiction that the usucaption period has elapsed (1 year movables, 2 years land).
• CLAUSULA ARBITRARIA and CONDEMNATIO as in the REI VINDICATIO.
cards.old_front: Wie lautet die INTENTIO der ACTIO PUBLICIANA — auf welcher Fiktion beruht sie?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — ACTIO PUBLICIANA, pleas, ACTIO NEGATORIA
cards.front: Who can bring the ACTIO PUBLICIANA — and what must he prove?
cards.back:
1. Usucapients in cases of legal deficiency (acquisition from an unauthorised person, from a person of limited capacity, on a putative title).
2. Bonitarian owners (RES MANCIPI merely delivered by traditio by the civil-law owner).
3. Civil-law owners who acquired derivatively — advantage: no PROBATIO DIABOLICA.
• Proof: TRADITIO on the basis of a valid title; only the period of possession is lacking.
• Capacity to be sued/restitution as in the REI VINDICATIO.
cards.old_front: Wer kann die ACTIO PUBLICIANA erheben — und was muss er beweisen?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — ACTIO PUBLICIANA, pleas, ACTIO NEGATORIA
cards.front: What is the EXCEPTIO IUSTI DOMINII?
cards.back:
Defence of the quirite owner against the ACTIO PUBLICIANA: SI EA RES NUMERII NEGIDII NON SIT — if the thing does not belong to the defendant.
• If he proves his ownership, the action fails → the usucapient (acquisition from a non-owner) is weaker than the present owner.
cards.old_front: Was ist die EXCEPTIO IUSTI DOMINII?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — ACTIO PUBLICIANA, pleas, ACTIO NEGATORIA
cards.front: What is a REPLICATIO? When does the REPLICATIO REI VENDITAE ET TRADITAE help?
cards.back:
REPLICATIO = the plaintiff's counter-plea against an EXCEPTIO.
• If the bonitarian owner sues his predecessor (still quirite owner) with the ACTIO PUBLICIANA and the latter raises the EXCEPTIO IUSTI DOMINII, the plaintiff obtains the REPLICATIO REI VENDITAE ET TRADITAE: AUT SI NUMERIUS NEGIDIUS FUNDUM … AULO AGERIO VENDIDIT ET TRADIDIT.
• Ground of acquisition other than purchase → REPLICATIO DOLI.
• Consequence: the transferor retains only a NUDUM IUS QUIRITIUM.
cards.old_front: Was ist eine REPLICATIO? Wann hilft die REPLICATIO REI VENDITAE ET TRADITAE?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — ACTIO PUBLICIANA, pleas, ACTIO NEGATORIA
cards.front: Bonitarian vs quirite owner in litigation — how does the bonitarian owner prevail (action and defence)?
cards.back:
As plaintiff: ACTIO PUBLICIANA; against the transferor's EXCEPTIO IUSTI DOMINII → REPLICATIO REI VENDITAE ET TRADITAE (or REPLICATIO DOLI).
As defendant: against the REI VINDICATIO of the quirite owner → EXCEPTIO REI VENDITAE ET TRADITAE or EXCEPTIO DOLI.
• Result: the bonitarian owner is stronger; the transferor is left with the NUDUM IUS QUIRITIUM.
cards.old_front: Bonitarischer vs quiritischer Eigentümer im Prozess — wie setzt sich der bonitarische Eigentümer durch (Klage und Abwehr)?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — ACTIO PUBLICIANA, pleas, ACTIO NEGATORIA
cards.front: What does convalescence mean — Pomponius (Iulianus) D 21.3.2 (Case 130)?
cards.back:
Retroactive curing of a legal deficiency.
• T buys land belonging to S from Titius and receives it; S dies, Titius inherits from him → by convalescence T becomes bonitarian owner (as in acquisition from the owner).
• Titius has only the NUDUM IUS QUIRITIUM; if he sells and delivers the land, having regained it, to Maevius, he cannot confer bonitarian ownership on him (NEMO PLUS IURIS …) → T's ACTIO PUBLICIANA against M succeeds.
• Cf Ulpian D 44.4.4.32 (Case 131).
cards.old_front: Was bedeutet Konvaleszenz — Pomponius (Iulianus) D 21.3.2 (Case 130)?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — ACTIO PUBLICIANA, pleas, ACTIO NEGATORIA
cards.front: Neratius D 19.1.31.2 (Case 133) vs Ulpianus (Iulianus) D 6.2.9.4 (Case 132): An unauthorised person sells the same thing successively to A and B — who has the ACTIO PUBLICIANA? And with two different unauthorised persons?
cards.back:
The same unauthorised person: Neratius — whoever received delivery first (parallel to the double sale by the owner and to convalescence; analogy).
Two different unauthorised persons: Neratius — likewise whoever received delivery first. Julian and Ulpian (Case 132) — whoever POSSESSES, regardless of whether delivery was made to him first or later.
• Classical controversy (also in the exam materials).
cards.old_front: Neratius D 19.1.31.2 (Case 133) vs Ulpianus (Iulianus) D 6.2.9.4 (Case 132): Ein Nichtberechtigter verkauft dieselbe Sache nacheinander an A und B — wer hat die ACTIO PUBLICIANA? Und bei zwei verschiedenen Nichtberechtigten?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — ACTIO PUBLICIANA, pleas, ACTIO NEGATORIA
cards.front: What is the purpose of the ACTIO NEGATORIA — what are immissions?
cards.back:
Action of the owner when a third party claims a servitude or another right in rem in his thing: declaration that the right does not exist, and restoration of the former state.
• Also against immissions = continuous disturbing interference from the neighbouring land (smell from a cheese dairy, smoke/steam, stone chips; Ulpian D 8.5.8.5, Case 134).
cards.old_front: Wozu dient die ACTIO NEGATORIA — was sind Immissionen?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — ACTIO PUBLICIANA, pleas, ACTIO NEGATORIA
cards.front: What does the INTERDICTUM QUOD VI AUT CLAM prevent?
cards.back:
Detrimental changes to the land made by a third party by force (VI — understood broadly: against a prohibition, Ulpian (Q. Mucius) D 43.24.1.5) or secretly (CLAM), e.g. dumping rubbish, poisoning a well.
• First remedy when the disturber does NOT claim a right to interfere (otherwise ACTIO NEGATORIA).
cards.old_front: Was verhindert das INTERDICTUM QUOD VI AUT CLAM?

cards.front: [Textbook Ex 43] Bellona sells and delivers to Ago a piece of land belonging to Carus; Ago is in good faith and builds a house on it for 10,000. 15 months after Ago acquired possession, Carus vindicates and refuses to pay for the house because he only wanted a vegetable garden. Claims?
cards.back:
• Ago is not owner: no derivative acquisition; usucaption (land 2 years) not completed after 15 months → Carus' REI VINDICATIO is well founded.
• Ago (in good faith when building): EXCEPTIO DOLI → retention until reimbursement of expenses, at most the increase in value (Celsus D 6.1.38).
• If Carus will not or cannot pay: Ago's IUS TOLLENDI (demolition, removal of the material); Carus can avert it by paying the demolition value; no chicanery.
• If Ago lost possession, as usucapient he would have the ACTIO PUBLICIANA — but it would fail against Carus (EXCEPTIO IUSTI DOMINII).
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 43] Bellona verkauft und übergibt Ago ein Grundstück des Carus; Ago ist gutgläubig und baut darauf um 10.000 ein Haus. 15 Monate nach Besitzerwerb vindiziert Carus und weigert sich, für das Haus zu zahlen, weil er nur einen Gemüsegarten wollte. Ansprüche?

cards.front: [Textbook Ex 44a/b] Leo wants to vindicate his vase against Melitta. (a) What if Melitta refuses the LITIS CONTESTATIO? (b) After the LITIS CONTESTATIO, before judgment, a landslide destroys Melitta's house together with the vase — consequences for ownership and the proceedings?
cards.back:
(a) Leo CANNOT compel Melitta to defend the REI VINDICATIO (ACTIONES IN REM impose no duty to defend). He brings the ACTIO AD EXHIBENDUM (vase = movable thing; for land INTERDICTUM QUEM FUNDUM): if Melitta does not produce the vase IN IURE → condemnation to the value of the thing; if she produces it but refuses to defend → the praetor allows Leo to take the vase away. (Textbook p. 161)
(b) With its destruction, ownership of the vase is extinguished. Chance (CASUS) after the LITIS CONTESTATIO: Sabinians — Melitta no longer possesses and is not at fault → acquittal; Proculians (RESTITUERE) — liability even for chance → condemnation to the value.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 44a/b] Leo will gegen Melitta seine Vase vindizieren. (a) Was, wenn Melitta die LITIS CONTESTATIO verweigert? (b) Nach der LITIS CONTESTATIO, vor Urteil, zerstört ein Erdrutsch Melittas Haus samt Vase — Folgen für Eigentum und Prozess?

cards.front: [Textbook Ex 44c] Melitta deliberately destroys Leo's vase BEFORE the LITIS CONTESTATIO because she expects his REI VINDICATIO. What applies?
cards.back:
• The REI VINDICATIO fails for lack of possession and of the thing; the fiction of possession (PRO POSSESSIONE DOLUS EST) applies to fraudulently defending the action or giving up possession AFTER the LITIS CONTESTATIO.
• Leo has a claim for damages under the LEX AQUILIA (culpable destruction before the LC).
• (The ACTIO AD EXHIBENDUM also covers whoever has fraudulently ceased to possess — QUI DOLO DESIIT POSSIDERE.)
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 44c] Melitta zerstört Leos Vase absichtlich VOR der LITIS CONTESTATIO, weil sie mit seiner REI VINDICATIO rechnet. Was gilt?

cards.front: [Textbook Ex 45] Without authority, Gripus sells and delivers a horse (not stolen) to Flora, who is in good faith. Two days later Helena steals it and sells it to Isauricus. Can Flora sue Isauricus? What if Isauricus is the true (quirite) owner?
cards.back:
• Flora is a usucapient (RES HABILIS, title purchase, BONA FIDES, possession); the period (1 year) has not elapsed; through the theft she loses possession.
• Against Isauricus: ACTIO PUBLICIANA — she would be owner after one year's possession; Isauricus has no better right (acquired from the thief, RES FURTIVA) → success.
• If Isauricus is quirite owner: EXCEPTIO IUSTI DOMINII → Flora's action fails (she did not acquire from him). Isauricus must, however, raise and prove the defence himself.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 45] Gripus verkauft und übergibt unbefugt ein nicht gestohlenes Pferd an die gutgläubige Flora. Zwei Tage später stiehlt Helena es und verkauft es an Isauricus. Kann Flora gegen Isauricus klagen? Was, wenn Isauricus der wahre (quiritische) Eigentümer ist?

cards.front: [Textbook Ex 46] Japyx sells and delivers his favourite slave Stichus to Cassandra. A week later Stichus flees back to Japyx and asks to be allowed to stay; Japyx refuses to hand him over. Possession and ownership? Which action does Cassandra have?
cards.back:
• Slave = RES MANCIPI, merely delivered by traditio → Cassandra becomes bonitarian owner (and possessor); Japyx retains only the NUDUM IUS QUIRITIUM.
• Flight: SERVUS FUGITIVUS — Cassandra retains possession SOLO ANIMO until a third party takes possession of him; with Japyx' refusal/taking over, Japyx acquires possession and Cassandra loses it (usucaption interrupted).
• Cassandra: ACTIO PUBLICIANA against Japyx; against his EXCEPTIO IUSTI DOMINII the REPLICATIO REI VENDITAE ET TRADITAE → she prevails.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 46] Japyx verkauft und übergibt seinen Lieblingssklaven Stichus an Cassandra. Eine Woche später flieht Stichus zu Japyx zurück und bittet, bleiben zu dürfen; Japyx weigert sich, ihn herauszugeben. Besitz und Eigentum? Welche Klage hat Cassandra?

cards.front: [Textbook Ex 47] Nike sells and delivers to Orion a piece of land belonging to her uncle Pius. A year later Pius dies and Nike inherits from him. Orion travels to Greece and asks Nike to look after the land; Nike sells it in her own name to Quinta, who is in good faith. Three months later Quinta is farming it. Ownership over time? Which action does Orion have against Quinta?
cards.back:
• Initially: Pius owner; Orion only usucapient (acquisition from an unauthorised person; land: 2 years).
• Death of Pius, Nike heir: convalescence → Orion becomes bonitarian owner; Nike has only the NUDUM IUS QUIRITIUM (Pomponius (Iulianus) D 21.3.2, Case 130).
• Nike as caretaker = Orion's detentor; her sale to Quinta cannot confer bonitarian ownership on Quinta (NEMO PLUS IURIS …); Quinta obtains only possession.
• Orion: ACTIO PUBLICIANA against Quinta — successful, as in Case 130.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 47] Nike verkauft und übergibt Orion ein Grundstück ihres Onkels Pius. Ein Jahr später stirbt Pius, Nike beerbt ihn. Orion reist nach Griechenland und bittet Nike, das Grundstück zu betreuen; Nike verkauft es im eigenen Namen an die gutgläubige Quinta. Drei Monate später bewirtschaftet Quinta es. Eigentum im Verlauf? Welche Klage hat Orion gegen Quinta?

cards.front: [Textbook Ex 48] Tiro buys from Verres the physician slave Stichus (earns 5,000/month). Two months after delivery Tiro learns that Verres was not the owner. Four months later the owner Claudia sues. Stichus at first continues working; one month after the LITIS CONTESTATIO Tiro forbids him to work; three months later the proceedings end. To what will the IUDEX condemn Tiro?
cards.back:
• Claudia is owner (Verres unauthorised; 6 months < 1 year → no usucaption).
• CLAUSULA ARBITRARIA: first an order to restore — Stichus together with the yields; otherwise CONDEMNATIO to QUANTI EA RES ERIT.
• Yields since LC (RESTITUERE): 1 month gathered (5,000, FRUCTUS PERCEPTI) + 3 months not gathered (15,000, FRUCTUS PERCIPIENDI) = 20,000 in addition to the value of the slave.
• Before the LC: months 1–2 in good faith → Tiro acquires the earnings. Months 3–6 after learning the truth: according to Pomponius/Paulus no further acquisition of fruits (restitution, possibly CONDICTIO FURTIVA/ACTIO FURTI); according to Julian continued acquisition until the action is brought.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 48] Tiro kauft von Verres den Arzt-Sklaven Stichus (verdient 5.000/Monat). Zwei Monate nach der Übergabe erfährt Tiro, dass Verres nicht Eigentümer war. Vier Monate später klagt die Eigentümerin Claudia. Stichus arbeitet zunächst weiter; einen Monat nach der LITIS CONTESTATIO verbietet Tiro ihm die Arbeit; drei Monate später endet der Prozess. Wozu wird der IUDEX Tiro verurteilen?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Servitudes (SERVITUTES), EMPHYTEUSIS, SUPERFICIES
cards.front: What are servitudes (SERVITUTES)?
cards.back:
Limited rights in rem in another's thing that oblige the owner to permit the holder to exercise a right or to refrain from exercising a right of his own (§ 482 ABGB).
• Classification: praedial servitudes (rural and urban) and personal servitudes.
cards.old_front: Was sind Servituten (Dienstbarkeiten)?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Servitudes (SERVITUTES), EMPHYTEUSIS, SUPERFICIES
cards.front: What does SERVITUS IN FACIENDO CONSISTERE NEQUIT mean — what exception is there?
cards.back:
A servitude cannot create a duty to act — only to tolerate or to refrain.
• Exception: SERVITUS ONERIS FERENDI — the owner of the servient building must keep it in the state of repair it was in when the servitude was created (Ulpian D 8.5.6.2, Case 142).
cards.old_front: Was bedeutet SERVITUS IN FACIENDO CONSISTERE NEQUIT — welche Ausnahme gibt es?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Servitudes (SERVITUTES), EMPHYTEUSIS, SUPERFICIES
cards.front: NULLI RES SUA SERVIT — what follows from this?
cards.back:
No one has a servitude in his own thing (Paulus D 8.2.26).
• If the holder acquires ownership of the burdened thing, the servitude is extinguished (CONFUSIO — merger of the holder and the person bound; not to be confused with mixing).
cards.old_front: NULLI RES SUA SERVIT — was folgt daraus?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Servitudes (SERVITUTES), EMPHYTEUSIS, SUPERFICIES
cards.front: What is a praedial servitude — who is entitled?
cards.back:
A right of the current owner of a piece of land in another piece of land that enables or facilitates the use of his own; tied to the land, transferable only together with it (today: easement).
• PRAEDIUM DOMINANS (dominant land), PRAEDIUM SERVIENS (servient land).
• E.g. Gallicus/Lysippe: the right of way passes along with the field when it is sold to Niketas; the buyer of Lysippe's estate acquires it burdened.
cards.old_front: Was ist eine Grunddienstbarkeit (Prädialservitut) — wer ist berechtigt?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Servitudes (SERVITUTES), EMPHYTEUSIS, SUPERFICIES
cards.front: Name the rural praedial servitudes (SERVITUTES PRAEDIORUM RUSTICORUM).
cards.back:
• Rights of way: ITER (walking, riding), ACTUS (driving cattle), VIA (driving vehicles)
• Water rights: AQUAE DUCTUS (conducting water across another's land), AQUAE HAUSTUS (drawing water)
• Right of pasture: IUS PASCENDI
cards.old_front: Nenne die ländlichen Prädialservituten (SERVITUTES PRAEDIORUM RUSTICORUM).

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Servitudes (SERVITUTES), EMPHYTEUSIS, SUPERFICIES
cards.front: Name the urban praedial servitudes (SERVITUTES PRAEDIORUM URBANORUM).
cards.back:
• Building servitudes: IUS ALTIUS NON TOLLENDI (not to build higher), IUS LUMINIS (light/view)
• Support rights: IUS TIGNI IMMITTENDI (inserting beams), IUS ONERIS FERENDI (resting one's building on the neighbouring building)
• Drainage rights: IUS STILLICIDII (dripping eaves), IUS FLUMINIS (diverting rainwater), IUS CLOACAE (sewage)
cards.old_front: Nenne die städtischen Prädialservituten (SERVITUTES PRAEDIORUM URBANORUM).

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Servitudes (SERVITUTES), EMPHYTEUSIS, SUPERFICIES
cards.front: What role do VICINITAS and UTILITAS play in praedial servitudes?
cards.back:
VICINITAS: the servient and dominant land should be neighbouring (Ulpian D 8.3.5.1, Case 143).
UTILITAS: the servitude must benefit the dominant land and exists only to the extent that this is actually the case.
• Paulus D 8.1.8 pr (Case 145): a right to go for walks or to dine on the neighbouring estate is not a servitude — it serves merely personal pleasure.
cards.old_front: Welche Rolle spielen VICINITAS und UTILITAS bei Prädialservituten?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Servitudes (SERVITUTES), EMPHYTEUSIS, SUPERFICIES
cards.front: How is a servitude to be exercised (SERVITUS CIVILITER EXERCENDA EST)?
cards.back:
Considerately — with the least possible impairment of the servient land; and only to its original extent (no unilateral extension).
• E.g.: whoever may water 20 sheep may not water 40 (Ulpian D 43.20.1.18, Case 140); against the additional ones the owner may block the way or bring the ACTIO NEGATORIA.
cards.old_front: Wie ist eine Servitut auszuüben (SERVITUS CIVILITER EXERCENDA EST)?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Servitudes (SERVITUTES), EMPHYTEUSIS, SUPERFICIES
cards.front: What are personal servitudes — how does Paulus define USUSFRUCTUS?
cards.back:
Rights in rem of a specific person, which are extinguished upon his death.
• Paulus D 7.1.1: USUSFRUCTUS EST IUS ALIENIS REBUS UTENDI FRUENDI SALVA RERUM SUBSTANTIA — the right to use another's things and take their fruits while preserving their substance (cf § 509 ABGB).
• Comprises USUS and FRUCTUS, also FRUCTUS CIVILES (rent).
• E.g. Hera: may live in the house or let it, but not convert it into a guesthouse.
cards.old_front: Was sind persönliche Dienstbarkeiten — wie definiert Paulus den USUSFRUCTUS?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Servitudes (SERVITUTES), EMPHYTEUSIS, SUPERFICIES
cards.front: Does the child of a slave woman held in usufruct belong to the usufructuary? And the young of an animal?
cards.back:
PARTUS ANCILLAE is not a fruit → belongs to the owner of the slave woman (Ulpian (Brutus) D 7.1.68 pr, Case 149).
• The young of animals are fruits → belong to the usufructuary of the mother animal (D 7.1.68.1).
cards.old_front: Gehört das Kind einer Sklavin im Nießbrauch dem Fruchtnießer? Und das Junge eines Tieres?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Servitudes (SERVITUTES), EMPHYTEUSIS, SUPERFICIES
cards.front: Usufruct of a herd (UNIVERSITAS RERUM) — what does “preserving the substance” mean?
cards.back:
The usufructuary must maintain the stock: replace animals that have died or been slaughtered with young animals (Ulpian D 7.1.68.2; Pomponius D 7.1.69).
• UNIVERSITAS RERUM = physically independent things combined into an aggregate that can be sold, pledged or sued for as a whole; it continues to exist even when individual animals die or are born.
cards.old_front: Nießbrauch an einer Herde (UNIVERSITAS RERUM) — was heißt „Erhaltung der Substanz“?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Servitudes (SERVITUTES), EMPHYTEUSIS, SUPERFICIES
cards.front: What is the CAUTIO USUFRUCTUARIA?
cards.back:
A formal promise by the usufructuary at the outset to use the thing at the discretion of an honest man (BONI VIRI ARBITRATU) — compensation for the owner's restricted rights.
• Usufruct usually arose by legacy (e.g. provision for the widow without appointing her heir).
cards.old_front: Was ist die CAUTIO USUFRUCTUARIA?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Servitudes (SERVITUTES), EMPHYTEUSIS, SUPERFICIES
cards.front: Usufruct vs loan for use, hire, usufructuary lease — difference?
cards.back:
USUSFRUCTUS is a right in rem (ACTIO IN REM).
Loan for use (gratuitous use), hire (use against payment), usufructuary lease (use against payment + taking of fruits) are contracts — only ACTIONES IN PERSONAM.
cards.old_front: Nießbrauch vs Leihe, Miete, Pacht — Unterschied?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Servitudes (SERVITUTES), EMPHYTEUSIS, SUPERFICIES
cards.front: What other personal servitudes are there?
cards.back:
• USUS: only use, no fruits (tendency to allow fruits for personal needs: D 7.8.12.1; Hadrian in Pomponius D 7.8.22 pr).
• HABITATIO (right of residence).
• OPERAE SERVORUM / OPERAE ANIMALIUM (services of slaves or animals).
cards.old_front: Welche weiteren persönlichen Dienstbarkeiten gibt es?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Servitudes (SERVITUTES), EMPHYTEUSIS, SUPERFICIES
cards.front: How is the holder of a servitude protected? What is the ACTIO CONFESSORIA?
cards.back:
1. He is not a proprietary possessor, but is protected by the praetor through special interdicts modelled on the possessory interdicts (e.g. INTERDICTUM UTI POSSIDETIS UTILE for the usufructuary of land).
2. Action in rem: VINDICATIO SERVITUTIS = ACTIO CONFESSORIA — declaration that the servitude exists + establishment of the lawful state.
• Counterpart of the ACTIO NEGATORIA (declaration that it does not exist).
cards.old_front: Wie wird der Servitutsberechtigte geschützt? Was ist die ACTIO CONFESSORIA?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Servitudes (SERVITUTES), EMPHYTEUSIS, SUPERFICIES
cards.front: What is the USUCAPIO LIBERTATIS?
cards.back:
Usucaption of freedom from a servitude by the owner if the holder does not exercise it for a certain period (NON USUS) — neither himself nor through others: 1 year for movables, 2 years for land.
• For building servitudes the owner must in addition create a state openly contrary to the servitude (e.g. building higher despite a SERVITUS ALTIUS NON TOLLENDI; Gaius D 8.2.6, Case 147).
• Not to be confused with usucaption of a servitude (the LEX SCRIBONIA prohibits the usucaption of praedial servitudes).
• Today § 1488 ABGB (3 years).
cards.old_front: Was ist die USUCAPIO LIBERTATIS?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Servitudes (SERVITUTES), EMPHYTEUSIS, SUPERFICIES
cards.front: Why is the term “legal servitude” misleading? Example?
cards.back:
In content like servitudes (restriction of ownership in favour of the neighbours), but formally created not by agreement but directly by law.
• E.g.: right to collect, every other day, fruit that has fallen over the fence — INTERDICTUM DE GLANDE LEGENDA (Law of the Twelve Tables).
• Modern: emergency right of way (NotwegeG 1896).
cards.old_front: Warum ist der Begriff „Legalservitut“ irreführend? Beispiel?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Servitudes (SERVITUTES), EMPHYTEUSIS, SUPERFICIES
cards.front: What is EMPHYTEUSIS (hereditary lease) — how is the emphyteuta protected?
cards.back:
An alienable and heritable right in rem to use land against annual rent; position similar to that of an owner (difference: duty to pay rent).
• Originally on public land (AGER VECTIGALIS; action ACTIO VECTIGALIS).
• Protection: interdicts; action in rem REI VINDICATIO UTILIS.
cards.old_front: Was ist die EMPHYTEUSIS (Erbpacht) — wie wird der Emphyteuta geschützt?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Servitudes (SERVITUTES), EMPHYTEUSIS, SUPERFICIES
cards.front: What is SUPERFICIES (building right) — how is the superficiary protected?
cards.back:
An alienable and heritable right to build on another's land against rent.
• Protection: INTERDICTUM DE SUPERFICIEBUS; in part an ACTIO IN FACTUM in rem (ACTIO DE SUPERFICIE).
• Modern: BaurechtsG 1912.
cards.old_front: Was ist die SUPERFICIES (Baurecht) — wie wird der Superficiar geschützt?

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Servitudes (SERVITUTES), EMPHYTEUSIS, SUPERFICIES
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 49] Brontes has granted Klio the right to rest her building on his (SERVITUS ONERIS FERENDI). What duties does Brontes have? What changes if Klio buys Brontes' land?
cards.back:
• Exception to the principle SERVITUS IN FACIENDO CONSISTERE NEQUIT: Brontes must maintain his building in the state it was in when the servitude was created, so that Klio's building can stand without damage (Ulpian D 8.5.6.2).
• If Klio buys the servient land, the servitude is extinguished: NULLI RES SUA SERVIT (CONFUSIO).

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Servitudes (SERVITUTES), EMPHYTEUSIS, SUPERFICIES
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 50] Carus' estate is burdened with a SERVITUS ACTUS in favour of his neighbour Daphne. Her heir Eros no longer drives the cattle along the path, but takes a shortcut through Carus' flower garden. Can Carus sue?
cards.back:
Yes.
• The praedial servitude is tied to the land and passes to Eros as the new owner.
• It must, however, be exercised considerately (CIVILITER) and only to its previous extent; unilateral extension is not permitted.
• Against the use of the flower garden: ACTIO NEGATORIA (and self-help by blocking it off, cf Ex 34 in the text).

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Servitudes (SERVITUTES), EMPHYTEUSIS, SUPERFICIES
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 51] Flora has a usufruct in Gripus' orchard. (a) Who owns the fruits? (b) May Flora convert the garden into a more profitable carrot field?
cards.back:
(a) Upon separation initially the owner Gripus; Flora acquires them only with PERCEPTIO (gathering, picking). If they fall into the hands of third parties beforehand, only Gripus can vindicate; Flora has the VINDICATIO USUSFRUCTUS against him.
(b) No — the USUSFRUCTUS applies SALVA RERUM SUBSTANTIA; she may only take the recurring yields, not alter the substance (cf Hera: may not convert the house into a guesthouse).

cards.topic: 17.11. Protection of ownership — Servitudes (SERVITUTES), EMPHYTEUSIS, SUPERFICIES
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 52] Japyx has a usufruct in a forest. (a) May he fell trees, and how many? (b) For 14 months the terminally ill Japyx cannot exercise his right; his heir Kassandra continues to exercise the usufruct. Has the servitude been extinguished?
cards.back:
(a) Only insofar as this is a recurring yield, without diminishing the substance of the forest (no clear-cutting) — preservation of the substance.
(b) Not by mere non-exercise: USUCAPIO LIBERTATIS for land only after 2 years of NON USUS (14 months are not enough).
• But: personal servitudes are extinguished upon the death of the holder → Kassandra does not inherit a usufruct; her exercise of it is without legal basis.

cards.front: [Textbook Ex 31, p. 161] Thetis and Querelus have long been disputing ownership of a valuable necklace that Thetis possesses. At night Querelus secretly takes it. Who can bring a REI VINDICATIO against whom — and what should Thetis do?
cards.back:
BOTH have capacity to sue, since both assert quirite ownership. Querelus has capacity to be sued: he has the necklace and intends to possess it — he is the possessor.
• In relation to Thetis, however, he possesses CLAM (secretly taken) → flawed possession.
• Since in proceedings IN REM the plaintiff bears the burden of proof, the role of defendant is more favourable → Thetis should first recover possession with the INTERDICTUM UTRUBI; then Querelus would have to sue and prove his ownership.
